title: 2007 HMMT February Guts Problem 19
statement:
Define \(x \star y=\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}+3 x y+y^{2}-2 x-2 y+4}}{x y+4}\). Compute

\[((\cdots((2007 \star 2006) \star 2005) \star \cdots) \star 1) .\]

solutions.text: \(\frac{\sqrt{\mathbf{1 5}}}{\mathbf{9}}\). Note that \(x \star 2=\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}+6 x+4-2 x-4+4}}{2 x+4}=\frac{\sqrt{(x+2)^{2}}}{2(x+2)}=\frac{1}{2}\) for \(x>-2\). Because \(x \star y>0\) if \(x, y>0\), we need only compute \(\frac{1}{2} \star 1=\frac{\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{2}+1-3+4}}{\frac{1}{2}+4}=\frac{\sqrt{15}}{9}\).
